description: Capabilities for the main window. IMPORTANT: this app has no local frontend at all — build.frontendDist and every window.url point at the live website — so a Capability's permissions are inert unless `remote` explicitly lists the origin actually loaded (Capability.local, defaulting to true, only covers Tauri's own asset:// local content). Without it, no permission below ever actually applies, regardless of what's listed — this is what a plain 'Command X not allowed by ACL' turned out to mean, even with a correct per-command permission defined. Both apex and www are listed: freqpanda.com itself sends a 308 redirect to www.freqpanda.com (confirmed by fetching it directly), so the webview's real, final origin is the www one even though tauri.conf.json's frontendDist/window.url are set to www.freqpanda.com already too — apex is kept here only as a safety net against ever pointing a URL at the bare domain again. Never a wildcard beyond this app's own domain, since remote+local-system access (fs, custom commands) is exactly the combination this field's own upstream doc comment warns about. SEPARATELY from the `remote` gotcha above: every #[tauri::command] in src/main.rs needs its own permission defined AND granted — two steps, both required, neither optional: (1) a src-tauri/permissions/<name>.toml file declaring '[[permission]] identifier = "allow-<kebab-case-command-name>"' + 'commands.allow = ["<command>"]' (Tauri does NOT auto-generate this for app-local commands the way it does for its own plugins — `cargo build` fails outright with 'Permission allow-x not found' if this step is skipped), and (2) that same identifier listed in this file's permissions array below (silently inert if skipped — no build error, just 'Command X not allowed by ACL' at runtime). local_training_status shipped with neither step done, silently masked because its only callers wrap the invoke in a try/catch with no user-facing error; run_local_backtest hit the identical gap, caught immediately since its caller does surface invoke errors. Whenever a new #[tauri::command] is added, do both steps for it in the same commit — see src-tauri/permissions/*.toml for the pattern.
